en.title: Call of Duty: Black Ops 2 Dominates PSN, Dethroning Fortnite
en.summary: A 14-year-old Call of Duty title has surprisingly surged to the top of PlayStation Network's most-played list in the US, unseating the perennial champion Fortnite. This unexpected resurgence highlights a powerful nostalgia and a persistent demand for classic gameplay.
en.body:
In a move that has sent ripples through the gaming community and likely caused a stir at Activision, **Call of Duty: Black Ops 2** has been dethroned Fortnite as the most-played game on PlayStation Network in the US. The data, compiled by Circana for the week ending July 18, reveals that a 2012 title, specifically a PlayStation 5 port of **Black Ops 2**, captured the top spot. This unexpected victory for a decade-old game over the current juggernauts of the live-service era, including **Fortnite**, **Call of Duty: Warzone**, and other recent entries in the franchise, is a testament to the enduring appeal of this particular entry.

**Black Ops 2** has long been a fan favorite, often cited as one of the best in the **Call of Duty** series for its compelling campaign, robust multiplayer, and innovative Zombies mode. The fact that it's not only still playable but *thriving* on the latest hardware, outperforming current-generation titles and even its own franchise siblings, raises fascinating questions about player preferences. Is this a resurgence driven by older players revisiting a beloved game from their youth, or are newer, younger gamers discovering its brilliance for the first time? The data suggests a potent combination of both, indicating a strong hunger for classic, well-crafted gaming experiences.

## The Appeal of a Classic

The dominance of **Black Ops 2** on the PSN charts is a stark reminder that polished gameplay and memorable content can transcend release dates. While publishers pour resources into the latest live-service models and battle royales, this data points to a significant segment of the audience that values the foundational elements of gaming. The success of **Black Ops 2** on the PS5 might also be attributed to Activision's efforts to make older titles accessible on current platforms, allowing a new generation to experience what made the franchise so popular. It’s a powerful statement from the player base, showcasing that nostalgia, combined with genuine quality, can indeed conquer the newest releases.

## What This Means for Gamers and Publishers

This shift in the charts is more than just a fleeting trend; it signifies a potent demand for classic experiences that resonates deeply with gamers. For publishers, it’s a clear signal that while the live-service model remains lucrative, the hunger for well-crafted, standalone or classic multiplayer experiences is undeniable. The fact that **Black Ops 1** also appeared on the list further underscores this point, suggesting a broader appetite for the **Black Ops** sub-series' unique blend of narrative and gameplay. This could influence future development strategies, potentially leading to more remasters, backward compatibility efforts, or even new titles that capture the spirit of these beloved older games.

## What's Next

With **Black Ops 2** proving its lasting power, players will undoubtedly continue to flock to its servers. The gaming landscape is always evolving, but this surge suggests that the classics are far from retired. We'll be watching to see if this trend continues as the summer's remaining major releases, such as **EA Sports College Football 25**, hit the market.

content_raw: A PS5 port of a Call of Duty game released in 2012 was recently the most-played title in the US on PlayStation Network, if you’re wondering how this summer of gaming releases is going. Black Ops 2 really is just that good, I guess. But also, wow. Fortnite is routinely the top-played game in the US across both PlayStation and Xbox, but the recent port of BO2 has taken PSN by storm in America, according to data gathered by Circana . Image via Circana I get it, because BO2 is easily my favorite CoD game of all time. But I can’t help but wonder how Activision feels seeing BO2 cannibalize the current game, Black Ops 7 , along with Warzone and other recent games. The publisher is still making money, I suppose, but the hunger for classics is definitely there, considering Black Ops 1 is also on the list, for the week ending July 18. BO2 being this popular on PS5 is very interesting to me. Are there that many old-heads (like myself) who grew up on the game, or is this a whole new generation of younger players who never got to experience it at its peak? I’m willing to bet it’s a combination of both. Fortnite remains king on Xbox for the same time period, along with Roblox , the Call of Duty HQ app, and Grand Theft Auto V . And so I can understand why publishers are all trying to capture that elusive live-service dragon, because the numbers are saying that’s what people are playing, and in droves. But also, wow, this is bleak. Where are all the new games? Oh, there’s EA Sports College Football 27 coming in at number 10. Silly me. Listen, I know summertime is usually a drought for new releases, but this list is shocking. Image via Activision I’m in a big gaming drought myself, so I’m looking forward to some big August releases like Beast of Reincarnation , Marvel Tokon: Fighting Souls , and Star Wars: Zero Company. Or maybe I will join the rest of PS5 folks and hit up BO2 for some good, old-fashioned CoD. What are you playing lately? Let us know in the comments, because this list has a whole lot of repeat offenders and I’m just waiting for some of the good new-new. 0 The post Fortnite just got dethroned as PlayStation’s top game by a 14-year-old Call of Duty appeared first on Destructoid .
